subject: Streaming performance: Locust staging access & IP warmup window
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Derek Hahn <derek.hahn@opto.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & immediate asks — streaming SLOs / staging access

Hi Derek — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned for the customer-led load run:  

Summary of performance targets discussed:
- Latency (non-streaming): 95th percentile <= 350 ms for single-turn text generation (prompt+response).
- Streaming token latency: aim for average per-token latency <= 120 ms; 95th percentile < 300 ms for steady-state.
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for single-turn scenarios (burst up to 220 req/s).
- Streaming concurrency: 250 concurrent streaming connections with token-per-second throughput equivalent to ~15k tokens/s overall.

Immediate asks from our side to enable the customer-run:  
1) Staging test account (API key + pre-shared secret) scoped to the staging environment.
2) IP allowlist entries for your test runners — we'll provide our egress IP ranges.
3) Please upload your approved Locust script (streaming plugin enabled) so we can sanity-run it on our staging infra before you start.
4) Confirm the preferred 3-hour window — our recommendation: Thu 19 Jul 2028, 09:00–12:00 PT.

I've attached a lightweight runner (rd_locust_staging_runner.py) that includes our recommended headers, backoff logic, and token-chunk pacing for streaming tests. If you can share your locustfile, we will validate it end-to-end in staging and pre-populate the allowlist.

Next steps:
- Derek: share locustfile and any auth details you need (OAuth vs API key).
- Ben: provision the staging key and firewall entries once Derek confirms his IPs.
- Marissa/Rishi: run a 15-minute smoke test on Wed 18 Jul to confirm handshake and KV cache priming.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & immediate asks — streaming SLOs / staging access

Thanks Jasmine — great summary. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the window:  

1) Auth: we'll use an API key for the staging run (simple bearer token). We prefer not to use OAuth for the test to reduce external dependencies.
2) Locust: attached is our current locustfile (opto_locustfile_v3.py). It uses the streaming plugin and a custom event hook to measure per-token latencies; includes a short ramp and long steady state.
3) IPs: we'll be running from our CI runners (AWS eu-west-1) and also a small set from our SF office — I'll enumerate the exact egress IPs by EOD today.
4) Window: Thu 19 Jul 09:00–12:00 PT works for us; please confirm the smoke test slot for Wed 18 Jul.

We will also need the staging endpoint URL (not prod) and any rate limits you plan to enforce so our script can be configured accordingly. Can you confirm if prefix caching is enabled in staging? That affects how we seed prompt prefixes for streaming.

I'll attach the locustfile now — please let me know if you need it adapted to your runner.

—Derek
Derek Hahn
Head of Infrastructure, Opto AI

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & immediate asks — staging provisioning & IPs

Copying internal ops notes here for the runbook we'll hand to security and infra:  

- Staging host to provide: staging.rdinference.net (TLS cert in place).
- Test account: generate one-time API key scoped to "opto-staging" with expiration 48 hours after the run.
- Allowlist entries (we will add these): 52.58.0.0/18, 3.125.0.0/16, plus the SF office IPs Derek will enumerate.
- Rate limits to set in staging for the run: soft limit 300 req/s, hard limit 500 req/s; per-key concurrency limit 500 connections. We'll monitor and throttle via our gateway if needed.
- Prefix caching: enabled by default in staging but warmed only if requested (we can preload via the runner). Recommend warming 30 common prefixes pre-run.

Marissa — can you provision the key and drop staging-test-credentials.txt into the secure share? Once Derek sends the IPs, I'll push them to the firewall and confirm.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Derek — we provisioned the staging key and placed it in the secure share (staging-test-credentials.txt). Ben has added the two CIDR blocks above; please reply with your SF office IPs and we will add them immediately.

Smoke test plan (Wed 18 Jul 16:00–16:20 PT):
- 5 min handshake: 1–2 connections to confirm TLS + headers and streaming chunking.
- 10 min short-run: ramp to 30 concurrent streaming connections to validate token-chunk pacing and prefix caching.
- 5 min cool-down and log capture.

Operational notes:
- Use staging API endpoint: https://staging.rdinference.net/v1/stream.
- Use the attached runner to enable KV cache warmup prior to the 10-minute run (see warmup() in runner).
- Please post logs to the shared Drive folder after the smoke test so we can review latencies and 95/99 quantiles.

We will be on Zoom during the smoke test and will escalate to infra if we see error rates >2% or token latencies exceeding the targets.

Thanks — looking forward to the handoff.
Jasmine
